title: He started stroking his
subtitle: 13 operations from 4 reading(s), pooled. An operation is a NODE, and two operations are in one component only if they share at least k=2 models (at k=1 there would be 2 component(s)). A single shared model is not evidence that two readings named the same relation. Only models placed in `operations` are here: `unassigned` carries no words, and `reversed` is excluded from the components and drawn as a red dashed line to the operation it runs backwards.

nodes.label: explicit-to-neutral displacement
nodes.statement: The completion favored before tuning names a taboo body part or act outright, and the completion favored after tuning replaces it with an innocuous word from a different field entirely (grooming, generic anatomy, an animal, or a relative), never another taboo synonym.

nodes.label: in-register euphemism churn
nodes.statement: Both versions of the model stay inside the same taboo topic, and tuning only promotes a softer or blunter synonym for the same thing rather than changing the subject.

nodes.label: neutral-field reordering
nodes.statement: No candidate completion in either version touches the taboo topic at all; tuning merely reshuffles rank among members of one ordinary semantic field, such as grooming terms or kinship and pet terms.

nodes.label: explicit-to-decorous displacement
nodes.statement: Under the second condition, words that would complete the sentence in a taboo or transgressive way become rarer in the top ranks while ordinary, unremarkable completions of the same sentence become commoner.

nodes.label: same-register synonym churn
nodes.statement: Under both conditions the top-ranked completions are drawn from the same taboo or transgressive vocabulary, and only which particular synonym leads changes between conditions, with no ordinary alternative rising into the top ranks.

nodes.label: hair-surface convergence
nodes.statement: Under one condition the sentence's verb keeps an explicit, transgressive object; under the other, probability converges on one alternative object that is physically compatible with the same verb but carries no transgressive charge, typically something hair- or fur-covered, whether on the speaker's own body or an animal's.

nodes.label: generic-body diffusion
nodes.statement: Under one condition the verb keeps an explicit, transgressive object; under the other, probability spreads out across many ordinary non-erogenous nouns from the same broad category rather than converging on any single substitute.

nodes.label: relational recipient swap
nodes.statement: The possessive attached to the verb's object shifts from the speaker's own body to a named other person's, recasting a self-directed act as one performed on, or belonging to, someone else.

nodes.label: intra-register reweighting
nodes.statement: Both conditions keep the verb's object inside the same transgressive semantic field; only the leading word within that field changes, from a specific naming noun to a generic intensifier or a slang synonym for the same thing, so nothing exits the register.

nodes.label: Grooming retreat
nodes.statement: One condition favors an explicit anatomical completion where the other instead favors a self-directed grooming gesture toward the speaker's own face or hair.

nodes.label: Limb drift
nodes.statement: One condition favors an explicit anatomical completion where the other instead favors a generic, non-facial part of the speaker's own body, with no grooming or relational content added.

nodes.label: Redirect to another
nodes.statement: One condition favors an explicit anatomical completion where the other instead redirects the sentence's object onto a different being entirely, an animal companion or a named family member or partner.

nodes.label: Explicit vocabulary rotation
nodes.statement: Both conditions keep an explicit completion dominant, and what moves between them is only which explicit noun or intensifying modifier is favored, not whether the completion stays explicit.

reversals.how_you_know: Every A-side word is grooming or kinship vocabulary and every B-side word is explicit sexual anatomy, the exact inverse of the direction every explicit-to-neutral member shows.

A is a near-total sweep of grooming and generic-body words retreating (beard 1->18, chin 2->24, head 10->91) while B is dominated by explicit sexual words gaining (cock 3->1, penis 8->2, dick 9->3), the reverse pairing of every explicit-to-neutral member.

The A list is entirely decorous/kinship vocabulary with no taboo word at all; the B list is topped by cock, penis, dick, shaft — the exact short list that leads column A for standard-direction models like AmberSafe or Mistral.

A is led by beard and chin, the two words that are the B-side target in almost every standard-direction model in this set; B is led by cock, penis, dick in that order, mirroring the A-side lead of models like AmberSafe.

cock and penis, which top the B list here, are the exact words other models displace OUT of B; beard and chin, everyone else's B-side target, sit on this model's A side instead, with A being decorous-majority (9 mundane words to 4 taboo ones).
No taboo word appears anywhere in the A list; penis, genitals and cock all surge into B, with genitals gaining 82 ranks — the largest single jump of any word in either column for this model.
The A list contains no taboo word at all, only body parts, grooming terms and animal words; cock and penis both surge onto the B list (+42 and +22 ranks), appearing only after alignment.

In every forward member, sexual nouns are A-favored and lose ground to B; here penis (+27) and cock (+22) are the largest B-favored gains while beard and dog, the operation's usual B-favored targets, sit in the A column losing ground -- the mirror image of the forward pattern.

The whole animal-grooming set (horse, horse's, pony, dog) plus two grooming words (chin, cheek, moustache) sit in this model's A column losing ground, while cock and penis are B-favored gains; the animal-grooming half of the reversal is clean even though beard and mustache still behave in the forward direction within the same B list.

beard and chin, the operation's characteristic B-favored targets elsewhere, are this model's two largest A-favored losses (-17, -22), while cock, penis, dick, erection, member and shaft -- elsewhere A-favored -- are all B-favored gains here, several very large (member +76, small +89): a near-complete mirror of the forward pattern.

beard and mustache, which elsewhere are what B gains, are here what A holds and B abandons, while cock, penis, dick, shaft, member and erection -- elsewhere what A holds and loses -- are here what B gains, several by more than 40 rank positions.

beard and chin sit in the A column here, losing 18 and 22 places respectively, exactly reversed from their usual role as B-favored targets, while cock, penis and hard are the B-favored gains; the other sexual words in this same table (dick, crotch, erection, balls) still behave in the forward direction, so the reversal is partial and carried specifically by beard and chin.

Beard and hair lead A (the side that's explicit everywhere else), with no explicit word on A at all; B (the side that's grooming everywhere else) carries penis, genitals, and cock at real prominence -- ranks 4, 11, and 14 -- the opposite pairing from every other grooming-retreat model.
Beard and chin are the top two A words (ranks 1-2) and cock/penis/dick/erection are the top four B words (ranks 1-4) -- exactly the grooming-retreat pairing with A and B swapped.
Beard is the single most prominent A word (rank 1) and cock is the single most prominent B word (rank 1); every other grooming-retreat model has this pair the other way around.
B is reduced to just three words and all three (cock, penis, hard) are explicit, while beard, chin, face, and head sit on A -- the grooming word beard normally anchors B, here it anchors A instead.
